name: performance
description: 8 scenarios x 3 context buckets (1K/8K/32K) x 10 targets = 240 measured rows in one jsonl; same target shares an identical question across buckets, only the context length differs; no scoring.

sampling.method: sha256(seed|upstream_id) ascending order + stratified largest-remainder quotas; independent of file row order

tokens_semantics: tokens = cl100k content tokens of messages[0].content + JSON-text cl100k tokens of tools (generic reference tokenizer, no chat template, no special tokens); messages_tokens/tools_tokens are the two audited parts
bucket_basis: declared cl100k content tokens target the calibrated budget for each (scenario, language, bucket) -- see budget_model; the raw bucket value is the run-side ISL target applied to the actual model-token count

tokenizer.name: cl100k_base
tokenizer.tokens_semantics: tokens = cl100k content tokens of messages[0].content + JSON-text cl100k tokens of tools (generic reference tokenizer, no chat template, no special tokens); messages_tokens/tools_tokens are the two audited parts

budget_model.target: cl100k content tokens (messages + tools JSON text)
budget_model.formula: budget = (bucket - RESERVE) / INFL (RESERVE=TOOL_RESERVE_CL if tools else PLAIN_RESERVE_CL; tools JSON is content and inflates with INFL)
budget_model.infl_semantics: content-type token-inflation coefficients: how many tokens a typical model tokenizer needs per cl100k token for this content type (empirically calibrated, generic content-type properties, not model-specific bindings)
budget_model.acceptance: declared tokens within floor(0.95*budget) .. floor(1.05*budget); the run-side +/-10% ISL band applies to actual model tokens vs the raw bucket

accept_rule: integer token counts: floor(0.95*budget) <= tokens <= floor(1.05*budget), where tokens = messages_tokens + tools_tokens (cl100k content tokens, no chat template) and budget is the calibrated per-(scenario, language, bucket) target (see budget_model)
accept_bounds_semantics: per-bucket construction acceptance around each row's calibrated budget (same +/-5% rule); these raw-bucket bounds are kept for reference: they are the basis of the run-side ISL tolerance, applied to actual model tokens, not to declared tokens

window_requirements.note: Runtime window check uses the target tokenizer's actual count (tokenized_prompt_tokens) + max_tokens + context_safety_margin + decode_guard_reserve; the declared cl100k budgets below are the calibrated approximation of that actual count. A 32,768-token window can only host actual counts <= 32526; remaining 32K rows are reported as not-testable (summary.skipped), never truncated.

deviations.note: Declared tokens are cl100k content tokens of the user message plus the JSON text of tools (chat-template control tokens excluded, no special tokens). The model-side rendered prompt differs: the runner appends a decode-guard message before chat-template overhead (see decode-guard-suffix) and every tokenizer counts text slightly differently, so actual input_context_tokens is calibrated via the budget model (see tokenizer-generic-cl100k), not by widening the band.

The construction tokenizer is cl100k_base (the OpenAI/industry-generic reference), not a model-specific tokenizer, so declared counts are model-agnostic. A target tokenizer can count the same content differently (more for code/math density, less for non-Latin scripts), so each row's declared count targets a calibrated cl100k budget: (bucket - RESERVE) / INFL, with one fixed model-side render reserve (TOOL_RESERVE_CL=270 when the row renders tools, PLAIN_RESERVE_CL=90 otherwise) and empirical content-type inflation coefficients INFL (0.50-1.21 by scenario/language), both calibrated on real-run evidence (240 cells, run 20261110T112641Z-8349). The tools JSON is content and inflates with INFL rather than being deducted separately (double deduction starved the 1K tool bucket: 796 actual vs the 921 band floor). Declared tokens therefore sit below the raw bucket by design so the actual rendered count lands centered in the run-side +/-10% ISL band. The coefficients are generic content-type properties, not bindings to any specific model.

At run time benchmark._apply_decode_guard appends a second user message (37 cl100k tokens) instructing the model to ignore the question above and write a >=250-word technical summary. The budget model already reserves these 37 tokens, so the guard does not push rendered prompts out of the ISL band. Generation follows the guard instruction, not the dataset question; this is a measurement-protocol deviation.
10 targets per scenario x bucket (240 measured requests total) is a load-shape profile for per-sample latency/TPS, not a leaderboard-scale evaluation: official benchmarks usually run every item.

Document scenarios use a character prefix of one LongBench v2 document per bucket (1K subset of 8K subset of 32K) with an identical question/options block; official LongBench v2 uses the full document with the official prompt template.

The document prefix is cut at a character offset, not at a structural boundary, so long_context prompts can end inside a JSON object/array/string and coding prompts can end inside an open Markdown code fence (for example 19/30 long_context rows have unbalanced braces). Structured closure of the sliced document is not guaranteed.
general_agent sends one BFCL v4 single-turn request with a target-first whole-function catalogue prefix; official BFCL scores multi-turn tool-call trajectories and exact arguments.

multilingual uses 10 different Global-MMLU questions rendered one per language (the same-language reference block is a load-shape extension), whereas the accuracy set and the official Global-MMLU protocol evaluate the same question in each language.
Performance rows carry no judge/gold contract: run mode never scores, SampleRecord.score stays null, and answer correctness is out of scope for this set.
instruction_following, math_logic and multilingual contexts are same-set reference blocks (other items rotated per target), not the official few-shot prompt templates.

Reference blocks are assembled from complete units (instruction / solved example / question) and then cut by character prefix, so the last unit can be partial: the final reference item may be half an instruction, half an example or half a question stem, and the cut may fall inside a multilingual question/option unit. The block is not repeated; only the tail unit is potentially truncated.

instruction_following renders each reference item as 'INSTRUCTION <k>: ids=<instruction_id_list JSON> kwargs=<kwargs JSON>' followed by the prompt. One pass of the 509 non-target items is ~43K cl100k tokens (> the calibrated 32K lower bound ~31,094), so the 32K reference block is a single non-repeating pass of distinct units (reference_pool_cycles is always 1); this replaces the earlier doubled block.

32K rows declare calibrated cl100k budgets (bucket/INFL - 37); with max_tokens=50 + 128 safety + 64 decode-guard = 242 reserved tokens a 32,768-token model window cannot host the upper rows (not-testable, reported as skipped, never truncated). The run-side window check uses the target tokenizer's actual count, which the budget model calibrates toward the bucket.
